title: the-slate-door-has-a-side-path
intention: A saveslate firing through the GENERIC seam CLI (python3 -m cairn.machines.skill_block fire saveslate <packet>) must either write the slate or refuse — never berth a firing that looks like a slate write while writing no slate.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-03 16:40, live at this session's own close: the generic CLI passed the saveslate contract, berthed the firing (saveslate-20260803T164057-836dac50249d), emitted a finding — and wrote NO slate file. The skill's own text claims 'there is no other path to the store'; true of the store, but the BERTH is the artifact downstream readers find, and a berth with no slate behind it is a close that looks recorded and is not — the exact shape of the 2026-07-24 'done that wasn't' correction. The real door (skills/saveslate/door.py) composes the seam and adds the write in one act; the generic path is the seam alone, and nothing marks the difference.
traces_to: Law 4 — the one-act write is the rule that matters; today it holds only when the caller picks the right command (policy)
Law 7 — the half-fired close is silent exactly where it must be loud

falsifier.proves_red: RED if the generic seam CLI can complete a saveslate firing without the slate existing on disk afterward — whether by refusing skills that declare a composing door, by delegating to it, or by another shape settled at the voyage; also RED if the fix breaks the generic path for skills that have no composing door (intent must keep firing bare).
falsifier.horizon: the next session close after the fix: the wrong command must fail loudly or do the whole act.

how: Fix the generic seam CLI so a saveslate firing through python3 -m cairn.machines.skill_block fire saveslate <packet> either writes the slate or refuses with a named lack — no silent pass-through.
watchme: none, because the falsifier is checkable in one proof run (fire the generic CLI for a skill with a composing door; assert refusal or the composed act)
sorted_berth: none, because filed directly at the TICKET door on measurement; casting completeness rides this field's own voyage — see ticket sorted-becomes-a-learning-block for the door this will answer to
intent_berth: none, because this is a TICKET-door bug entry (ruling 2026-08-02), not a born intention — the measurement above is the birth record
chart_claim: chart chain complete: validate-20260828T094344-f59b10651d43.json — all 7 stages berthed through gates. Two pieces: (1) route the generic CLI to the tenant's own fire path for saveslate, so the slate write runs; (2) a proof tooth asserting both berth and slate file exist after a generic-CLI firing. Order: routing first (solidify the layer), proof second.
entry_door: TICKET — a bug, measured live; editing lines fixes it (ruling 2026-08-02: a bug does not ride /intent)
filed_edges: [AKIEN] DOES THE GENERIC CLI LEARN ABOUT COMPOSING DOORS, OR DOES THE SKILL DECLARE ITSELF? If the CLI grows knowledge of which skills have a composing door, it stops being generic and takes on a second owner's business (Law 6). If a skill DECLARES 'I have a composing door — refuse me bare', the CLI stays dumb and the rule is the skill's own. The second is the standing house pattern (ask_user.sh's dumb gate; the renderer that must not sniff). Confirm it and the build is small; overturn it and say why, because the same pattern is load-bearing in two other places.
